title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a rewritten version of the summary at the end of the previous page. That earlier draft had inconsistent index labels (6, 4) and an unfinished (38)-(39); here they are replaced by a coherent prism-shaped lattice.

Context. In 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets', Grothendieck studies loops and relations in the fundamental groups of moduli stacks (the Teichmüller tower) and their rigidity under Galois actions. Here rho is a torsion element and L_rho = <rho> is cyclic of order 6, a group of order 6 such as the automorphism group of the j=0 elliptic curve. On the usual reading, N_rho^* is a normalizer and Z_rho a centralizer of this finite subgroup in a modular (mapping-class / Teichmüller-type) group.
- M^0(-J) ⊂ M'(-J), M'''(-J) are finite-index subgroups attached to a 'twisted' version (-J) of the modular group.
- mu is the central subgroup of order 2, presumably generated by the elliptic/hyperelliptic involution -1.
- D_rho = mu_12 · L_rho is the dihedral group of order 12; D_tau' (order 4) and mu_tau' (order 2) are its subgroups attached to an involution tau'.

Formula (36) records two decompositions as products of subgroups (semidirect type): M''' ≅ M'''(-J)·S^{+1} and N_rho^* ≅ M'''(-J)·L_rho.

The diagram (37) has the following rows:
- top: M^0(-J) ⊂_2 M'(-J) = Z^!_{rho,0} ⊂_2 M'(-J)×mu ⊂_3 Z_rho;
- middle: M'''(-J) ⊂_2 M'''(-J)×mu ⊂_2 N_rho^? ⊂_3 N_rho^*;
- finite levels: 1 ⊂_2 mu ⊂_3 L_rho, and mu_tau' ⊂_2 D_tau' ⊂_3 D_rho.
The slanted arrows are all of index 2: M^0 ⊂ M''', M' ⊂ M'''×mu, M'×mu ⊂ N^?, Z_rho ⊂ N^*, mu_tau' ⊂ ..., L_rho ⊂ D_rho.

The indices compose consistently: [N_rho^* : M^0(-J)] = 2·2·2·3 = 24, as stated in the text. So the lattice is that of the order-24 quotient N_rho^*/M^0(-J), with the finite groups L_rho and D_rho (order 12) mapping onto the 'horizontal' quotient pieces.

Grothendieck says this gives, intuitively, all the 'big' finite-index subgroups between M^0(-J) and N_rho^*. He announces that he will next settle which of them are normal in which, and identify the quotient groups. The next page does exactly this: it redraws the cube and notes that M'(-J)·mu_tau' is not a subgroup. It then proves that M'(-J)×mu and M^0(-J)×mu are characteristic in Z_rho, by describing them as Z_rho ∩ M^! and Z_rho ∩ M^! ∩ Ker(eps_2).

The purpose is bookkeeping on the structure of normalizers and centralizers of torsion in the modular groups. This is needed for the loop-equation / Galois-Teichmüller analysis: how a Galois or GT-type automorphism acts on the normalizer of a finite subgroup.
errors: No genuine mathematical error is visible: the index labels on this page compose consistently to 24.
The previous page's version of (37), with labels 6 and 4 and an unfinished (38)-(39), is inconsistent with this page and was evidently abandoned and redone here.
The vertex 'N_rho^?' carries an unresolved notation (the '?' is in the manuscript), so its definition is not determined on this page.
Calling the products 'M'''(-J)·L_rho' isomorphisms '≅' implicitly asserts semidirect-product decompositions, which are not justified on this page.

ideas.what: Lattice of finite-index subgroups between M^0(-J) and the normalizer N_rho^* of an order-6 torsion subgroup L_rho, with indices 2 and 3 (total index 24), arranged as a prism
ideas.modern_name: Structure of normalizers/centralizers of finite subgroups in mapping class (modular) groups; subgroup lattice of a finite quotient

ideas.where_published: Not in the published texts; only the general programme of studying the Teichmüller tower and its Galois action is in Esquisse d'un programme.

missed.claim: This is a detailed hand computation of the subgroup lattice of the normalizer of an order-6 torsion element in a (twisted) modular group. It serves to check which subgroups are characteristic and hence preserved by outer Galois/GT actions. The theme of torsion and normalizers in the Galois–Teichmüller setting was later developed independently, e.g. by Collas and Maugeais on torsion in GT and inertia at elliptic points. This page adds only bookkeeping, not a new result.
missed.quote: où nous trouvons ici (intuitivement) tous les "gros sous-groupes", c'est-à-dire des sous-groupes d'indice fini de N_ρ^*, intermédiaires entre celui-ci et M^0(-J) (d'indice 24 dans N_ρ^*)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. It documents that Grothendieck systematically analysed the normalizers of torsion in the modular tower, as a prelude to Galois-equivariance questions. The characteristic-subgroup arguments are standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds a corrected summary diagram of a finite subgroup lattice (index 24) plus a plan to study normality. This is routine group-theoretic bookkeeping inside a larger computation, with no new idea on the page itself.
transcription_corrections: In the diagram the top-row middle arrow goes M'(-J)=Z^!_{ρ0} ⊂_2 M'(-J)×μ, and M'(-J)×μ ⊂_3 Z_ρ. The previous-page labels 6 and 4 are not on this page.
'M_0(-J)' in the text should read M^0(-J) (superscript 0), as in the diagram.
'fers de sous-groupes' is doubtful; it more plausibly reads 'gros sous-groupes' (in quotes), though the reading is uncertain.
'question d'invariance de ces sous-groupes les uns dans les autres' is consistent with the image (normality question).
The last sentence plausibly reads 'Je vais refaire un diagramme qui montre mieux les relations [d'inclusion] entre les groupes en question', with a crossed-out word before 'relations'.
The bottom row is μ_{τ'} ⊂_2 D_{τ'} ⊂_3 D_ρ, with a slanted arrow 1 → μ_{τ'} labelled 2. The vertical arrows (e.g. Z_ρ ↔ L_ρ, M'(-J)×μ → μ) appear to be projections or inclusions.
In (36) the factor after M'''(-J) in the first line looks like a symbol with superscript '+1' (possibly 𝔖^{+1} or C^{+1}). It is uncertain.
